title: RevisionDojo vs Kognity: IB Platform Comparison
summary: Compare RevisionDojo vs Kognity for IB textbooks, practice, assignments, analytics, AI feedback, coursework, accessibility, and school pricing.
body_text: RevisionDojo and Kognity support IB learning in fundamentally different ways. Kognity is primarily a school-licensed digital textbook, assignment, and classroom analytics platform , while RevisionDojo combines independent revision, exam practice, AI feedback, and coursework support for students and schools . The better choice therefore depends on the problem being solved. Kognity is often stronger when a school wants a shared, centrally managed teaching resource. RevisionDojo is often stronger when students need an integrated system for independent revision, timed practice, feedback, and IA, EE, or TOK development. RevisionDojo vs Kognity: the short answer Choose Kognity if your priority is an official co-published textbook model, teacher-set assignments, class engagement data, and consistent implementation across departments. Kognity describes itself as the IB's only digital-first publishing partner and says it is used by one in three IB schools. These are Kognity's published claims , rather than findings from an independent head-to-head study. Choose RevisionDojo if the priority is exam preparation, targeted question practice, timed mock examinations, Jojo AI feedback, flashcards, and coursework workflows. Students can access RevisionDojo's IB resources independently, while schools can use classroom, assessment, and bulk-feedback features through RevisionDojo for Schools . Neither platform replaces teachers, current IB subject guides, or authenticated assessment procedures. Decision table Area RevisionDojo Kognity Likely better fit Core model Student and school platform for revision, practice, AI feedback, mocks, and coursework School-licensed interactive textbooks, assignments, practice, and analytics Depends on whether revision or curriculum delivery is the priority Curriculum content Syllabus-aligned notes, lessons, flashcards, questions, and exam resources Structured interactive textbooks covering supported DP subjects Kognity for textbook-led teaching; RevisionDojo for concise revision

title: After-Hours Patient Support: Capture 30–40% of Lost Revenue
summary: 30–40% of dental patient inquiries arrive after hours and go unanswered. Learn how AI-powered after-hours support captures this revenue in 2026.
body_text: The After-Hours Revenue Gap No One Talks About Picture this: it's 7:43 PM on a Tuesday. A parent just finished dinner, put the kids to bed, and finally has a quiet moment to call your practice about their child's toothache. They dial your number. They get voicemail. They hang up — and call the practice down the street that picks up. That scenario is playing out hundreds of times a week across dental practices nationwide, and the financial damage is staggering. According to recent data, 30–40% of patient inquiries occur outside business hours and are lost by practices relying on traditional call centers or online booking platforms that cannot handle complex inquiries. For a busy practice, that's not a minor inconvenience — it's a structural revenue leak that compounds every single day. In 2026, after-hours patient support has graduated from a "nice-to-have" amenity to a genuine competitive differentiator. The practices winning new patients, closing treatment plans, and building loyal patient bases are the ones that are reachable when patients actually have time to call. This guide breaks down why the after-hours window matters so much, what the staffing reality looks like, and exactly how forward-thinking practices are solving the problem without burning out their teams. Why After-Hours Calls Carry Outsized Revenue Potential The High-Intent Caller Phenomenon Not all phone calls are created equal. Patients who call after hours — during evening hours, lunch breaks, or school pickup windows — are often already primed to make a decision. They've done their research, they've felt the pain (sometimes literally), and they're ready to book. These aren't casual browsers; they're high-intent callers who have carved out a specific moment to take action. As noted in Patientdesk.ai's analysis of after-hours strategies , booking decisions increasingly happen during these off-peak windows — and callers in these moments carry purchase intent that rivals or exceeds daytime inquiries. When your practice fails to answer, you're not just losing a phone call. You're losing a patient who was ready to say yes. The Lifetime Value Math Let's put real numbers to this. A practice receiving just five after-hours calls weekly and converting two of those into new patients worth $2,000 each in lifetime value captures $208,000 in annual revenue through extended availability alone. That's not a projection built on optimistic assumptions — it's straightforward math based on modest conversion rates and average patient lifetime values. Meanwhile, no-shows and missed interactions carry their own cost. Research shows no-shows consume roughly 14% of a medical group's revenue on a given day , with annual revenue losses around $150,000 per physician. Every after-hours call that goes unanswered is a potential no-show that never even made it onto the schedule. The Treatment Acceptance Connection The revenue stakes are amplified by a troubling trend in case acceptance. Dental practices face a 47% treatment acceptance gap in 2026 , according to Titan Web Agency's comprehensive look at dental industry trends. That means nearly half of recommended treatment plans are never accepted — and a significant portion of that gap can be traced back to poor follow-up and missed touchpoints, including after-hours calls where patients were ready to commit. When a patient calls after hours to ask about a crown they've been putting off, that's not just a scheduling inquiry. It's a treatment acceptance opportunity. Letting it go to voicemail is letting revenue walk out the door. The Staffing Crisis Making Human Coverage Impossible A Breaking Point for Front Desk Teams Here's the uncomfortable truth about after-hours coverage in 2026: you can't staff your way out of this problem. The dental staffing shortage has reached a level that makes extended human coverage economically and practically unfeasible for most practices. Over 90% of dentists who attempted to recruit a dental hygienist in Q1 2026 said the process was either "very" or "extremely challenging" . Front desk and administrative roles face similar pressures. Asking existing staff to cover evening and weekend calls isn't just expensive — it's a fast track to burnout and turnover, which only deepens the staffing crisis. The math simply doesn't work. Hiring a dedicated after-hours receptionist means paying premium wages for overnight and weekend shifts, managing scheduling complexity, and still dealing with sick days and vacations. For most independent practices and even many DSOs, this is a non-starter. The Insurance Pressure Multiplier The staffing crisis doesn't exist in isolation. Insurance reimbursement pressure is cited by 55.3% of dentists as their number one issue in 2026 , squeezing margins at the same time that labor costs are rising. This creates a brutal double bind: practices need more revenue to survive, but they can't afford the staff to capture it. This is precisely why automation and AI receptionist tools have emerged as the primary solution. They don't require benefits, don't call in sick, and don't demand overtime pay for a 10 PM call on a Friday night. What Happens When Practices Do Nothing The consequences of leaving after-hours calls unanswered aren't abstract. Patients who reach voicemail don't wait patiently for a callback the next morning — they call a competitor. According to Helpware's 2026 patient experience research , practices should "consider extending the team with a specialized partner when demand fluctuates significantly, after-hours coverage becomes difficult to maintain, language requirements exceed internal capabilities, or key performance metrics such as hold times and response times continue to deteriorate despite hiring efforts." In other words, if your hold times are climbing and your after-hours calls are going unanswered, the answer isn't to push your existing team harder. It's to bring in a solution that scales without adding headcount. What Patients Actually Expect in 2026 The 24/7 Digital Access Standard Patient expectations have been permanently reset by consumer technology. The same person who can order groceries at midnight, book a flight at 6 AM, and stream a movie on demand expects their healthcare interactions to be similarly frictionless. 77% of dental patients prefer online scheduling when it is available , underscoring the depth of demand for 24/7 digital access. This isn't a generational quirk limited to younger patients. Across age groups, the expectation of immediate access has become normalized. When a practice can't meet that expectation, it doesn't just lose the immediate booking — it signals to the patient that the overall experience will be similarly inconvenient. Omnichannel Expectations Are Now Table Stakes It's not enough to simply be available after hours on one channel. According to Patient Prism's analysis of healthcare call center trends in 2026 , omnichannel communication has become table stakes: patients expect unified experiences across phone, chat, and web without having to repeat their story. Leading practices are consolidating platforms to give agents — human or AI — complete conversation history across every touchpoint. A patient who texted your practice at noon and then calls at 8 PM expects the evening interaction to reflect what was already discussed. Siloed systems that treat each channel as a separate conversation create friction that erodes trust and increases the likelihood of patient churn. Measuring Experience Beyond Surveys Traditional patient satisfaction surveys are struggling to keep pace with these expectations. The national CAHPS survey response rate was just 23% in CMS's April 2026 public report , highlighting the difficulty of measuring patient experience through traditional survey methods alone. Practices that rely solely on quarterly surveys to gauge after-hours satisfaction are working with a dangerously incomplete picture. The better signal is operational: track after-hours call answer rates, callback completion rates, and after-hours booking conversion. These metrics tell you far more about patient experience than a survey that only 23% of patients bother to complete. The AI-Powered After-Hours Solution Stack How Agentic AI Has Matured Beyond Simple Chatbots The AI tools available for after-hours coverage in 2026 bear little resemblance to the clunky chatbots of a few years ago. According to Patient Prism's healthcare call center industry report , AI-powered automation has matured beyond simple chatbots. Top practices now deploy agentic AI for after-hours coverage with intelligent escalation to human agents when clinical complexity or patient frustration is detected — balancing efficiency with the reality that patients trust doctors four times more than AI for medical decisions. This is the critical distinction: modern AI after-hours solutions aren't trying to replace human judgment for complex clinical situations. They're designed to handle the high volume of administrative and scheduling interactions that don't require clinical expertise, while recognizing when a situation needs a human touch and escalating accordingly. "Since patients demand convenience but trust humans for complex decisions, position your AI to cover after-hours periods and peak volume times. Trust evaporates with poor handoffs, so configure your AI to detect when it's reached its limits — whether from clinical complexity or rising patient frustration." — Patient Prism, 2026 Core Capabilities to Look For When evaluating an AI after-hours solution for your practice, the following capabilities separate effective tools from expensive disappointments: Real-time appointment scheduling — The AI should be able to book, reschedule, and confirm appointments directly in your practice management system, not just collect information for a callback PMS integration — Seamless connection with Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, and other major systems is non-negotiable; Patientdesk.ai's platform integrates directly with these systems for real-time scheduling, insurance verification, and payment collection Intelligent escalation — The system should detect frustration, clinical complexity, or urgent situations and route them appropriately rather than forcing every interaction through the same script Omnichannel coverage — Phone, web chat, and SMS should all feed into a unified conversation history HIPAA compliance — Any tool handling patient information must meet strict compliance standards; this is non-negotiable The Human Escalation Layer The most effective after-hours models in 2026 aren't purely automated — they're hybrid. AI handles the volume; humans handle the exceptions. Charta Health's analysis of urgent care trends notes that urgent care centers are investing heavily in AI tools and ambient listening technology to maintain throughput with lean staffing models, precisely because the hybrid model allows them to serve more patients without proportionally increasing headcount. For dental practices, this means configuring your AI to handle appointment scheduling, insurance questions, and general inquiries autonomously — while flagging calls involving dental emergencies, highly anxious patients, or complex treatment questions for immediate or next-morning human follow-up. Converting After-Hours Leads Into Accepted Treatment Plans The Follow-Up Gap Capturing an after-hours inquiry is only half the battle. The other half is converting that inquiry into a scheduled appointment and, ultimately, accepted treatment. This is where many practices drop the ball — they invest in after-hours coverage but fail to build the follow-up infrastructure that turns leads into revenue. Patientdesk.ai's AI Patient Sales Coordinator is specifically designed to address this gap, automatically following up with after-hours leads and high-intent callers to recover treatment plan revenue and improve case acceptance rates. Rather than relying on a busy front desk team to remember to call back every after-hours inquiry, the system handles follow-up systematically and at scale. Timing Is Everything The window for converting an after-hours inquiry is narrow. A patient who called at 9 PM and didn't get through is most receptive to a follow-up the next morning — not three days later when they've already booked with a competitor or talked themselves out of the treatment. Automated follow-up systems that trigger within hours of an after-hours inquiry dramatically outperform manual callback processes that depend on staff remembering to check a voicemail log. Connecting After-Hours Support to Treatment Acceptance The 47% treatment acceptance gap isn't just a scheduling problem — it's a communication and follow-up problem. Patients who express interest in treatment after hours and then receive no timely follow-up are far more likely to delay or decline. Practices that close this loop with systematic after-hours capture and automated follow-up are directly attacking the treatment acceptance gap at one of its most vulnerable points. Building Your After-Hours Support Strategy: A Practical Framework Step 1: Audit Your Current After-Hours Performance Before investing in any solution, understand your baseline. Pull your call data and answer these questions: How many calls come in after 5 PM and before 8 AM on weekdays? What percentage of those calls reach a live person or complete an online booking? How many after-hours voicemails receive a callback within 24 hours? What is your after-hours call-to-appointment conversion rate? Most practices are shocked by what this audit reveals. If you don't have the data to answer these questions, that itself is a finding — you're flying blind on a significant portion of your patient interactions. Step 2: Define Your Coverage Model Based on your audit, determine what level of after-hours coverage you need: AI-only coverage works well for practices with high volumes of straightforward scheduling and FAQ inquiries AI with human escalation is appropriate for practices with a meaningful volume of complex or urgent after-hours calls Outsourced answering service may be appropriate as a bridge solution while you evaluate AI options, though Helpware's guidance notes that specialized partners work best when paired with clear performance metrics and escalation protocols Step 3: Integrate With Your Existing Systems Any after-hours solution that operates in a silo will create more problems than it solves. Prioritize tools that integrate directly with your practice management software so that after-hours bookings appear in your schedule in real time, not as a batch of callbacks waiting for a staff member to manually enter them the next morning. Delta Dental's 2026 practice guidance emphasizes scheduling standards and patient access expectations as core components of practice success — and seamless system integration is foundational to meeting those standards consistently. Step 4: Train Your Team on the Hybrid Model Your front desk team needs to understand how after-hours AI coverage works and what their role is in the handoff. Clear protocols for reviewing after-hours interaction logs, following up on escalated calls, and handling patients who mention they "called last night" are essential for maintaining the seamless experience patients expect. Step 5: Measure, Iterate, and Optimize Set specific KPIs for your after-hours coverage from day one: After-hours answer rate (target: 95%+) After-hours booking conversion rate (benchmark against your daytime rate) Follow-up completion rate for escalated calls Revenue attributed to after-hours bookings (monthly and quarterly) Review these metrics monthly and adjust your configuration — escalation triggers, AI response scripts, follow-up timing — based on what the data shows. The Competitive Reality: What Happens If You Wait The practices that move on after-hours support now will build a structural advantage that compounds over time. Every month of unanswered after-hours calls is a month of patients going to competitors who are available. Every missed high-intent caller is a lifetime value of $2,000+ that walks out the door. The staffing crisis isn't going to resolve itself. Insurance reimbursement pressure isn't going to ease. And patient expectations for 24/7 access aren't going to retreat. The practices that thrive in this environment will be the ones that stopped waiting for conditions to improve and built the infrastructure to compete on availability. An AI booking system for dental practices that handles after-hours calls, appointment scheduling, and phone answering without additional front desk headcount isn't a futuristic concept — it's a deployable solution available today. The question isn't whether your practice needs after-hours support. The question is how much longer you can afford to go without it. Conclusion: After-Hours Support Is Now a Revenue Strategy After-hours patient support has completed its evolution from a customer service nicety to a core revenue strategy. With 30–40% of inquiries arriving outside business hours, a 47% treatment acceptance gap to close, and staffing shortages that make human coverage economically impossible, the case for AI-powered after-hours solutions has never been stronger. The math is clear. The technology is mature. The competitive pressure is real. Practices that implement intelligent after-hours coverage — with AI handling volume, smart escalation routing complex cases to humans, and systematic follow-up converting inquiries into accepted treatment — will capture revenue that their competitors are leaving on the table every single night. The patients are calling. The only question is whether you'll be there to answer.

title: Amazon's water conservation and replenishment efforts around the world
summary: Get the latest updates on how we’re reducing our water footprint and investing in innovations to address water scarcity.
body_text: March 19, 2025 2:00 AM Tackling global water scarcity: Amazon’s commitment to water replenishment Water sustains life on Earth, yet roughly half of the world’s population is experiencing severe water scarcity, with more than 2 billion people without access to safe drinking water. Every year on March 22, World Water Day emphasizes the importance of global collaboration to protect our most precious shared resource. For Amazon, this day also serves as an opportunity to raise awareness about global water challenges and showcase our investments and innovations aimed at addressing widespread water scarcity issues. Amazon now has more than 50,000 electric delivery vans globally. Meet the growing lineup of electric vehicles. From custom-built vans to e-cargo bikes, these zero-tailpipe-emission vehicles help deliver billions of packages to customers around the world. Conserving water in our operations and returning water to communities Amazon aims to be a good water steward everywhere it operates. For example, Amazon recently set a goal to replenish more water than we use across our India operations by 2027, and is committed to being “ water positive ” across all AWS data centers by 2030. We’re reducing our water footprint by increasing the efficiency of our water use throughout our operations while also investing in ways to replenish water in our communities. Some examples: Amazon is the largest corporate purchaser of renewable energy globally for the fifth year in a row With more than 600 projects worldwide, Amazon is also supporting solar and wind initiatives in regions with polluted grids to help curb emissions. Amazon scaled harvesting and reuse solutions in its fulfillment centers, sort centers, and delivery stations around the world. We’ve also created a global water metering and leak detection program, with one pilot in the United Kingdom saving an estimated 700 million liters of leaked water over two years. The Boss Defrost’s powerful circulating pump system recycles meltwater instead of letting it run down the drain. Whole Foods Market stores in the Denver area with Boss Defrost systems installed saw overall store water usage decrease by an average of 12% between 2021 and 2022. In many of its data centers AWS uses direct evaporative cooling and free-air cooling systems to remove heat from servers in data centers. Recycled water is also used for cooling at 24 data centers worldwide, preserving valuable drinking water for communities and the environment. Amazon’s global corporate offices are increasingly using recycled water and low-flow fixtures. For example, at HQ2 in Arlington, Virginia, by capturing and reusing rainwater, shower water, and HVAC condensate, the building is expected to achieve 50% water savings below building code , and recycle 7.5 million gallons each year. Globally, Amazon’s 27 water replenishment projects are expected to return more than 8 billion liters of water annually once completed. These projects expand access to clean water and sanitation, improve water quality, and increase the water available to water-stressed communities. Some of these projects are already under way, while others are just commencing. For example, earlier this month we announced three projects in Spain that are expected to reduce flood risk for 700,000 residents in the province of Zaragoza, modernize critical infrastructure, and optimize agricultural water use through artificial intelligence (AI). And in India, Amazon has invested in five projects, including partnering with the global nonprofits Water.org and WaterAid to bring clean water and sanitation to over 250,000 people surrounding our regions there. 01 / 05 Sharing what we’ve learned To help other companies take similar steps to reduce water usage, we’ve created a public water stewardship program playbook available through the Amazon Sustainability Exchange . This resource is meant to be a starter guide for any organization looking to establish a similar water stewardship program. Visit the water stewardship section of the Amazon Sustainability website to learn more. Innovate, collaborate, scale: Inside Amazon’s approach to decarbonizing its global network of buildings From fulfillment centers to data centers to grocery stores, we’re testing and scaling new tech to push toward net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.

title: AvePoint and Native: Express Protection for Entra ID
summary: See why Microsoft's native Entra ID backup and AvePoint work better together for faster recovery, longer retention, and stronger resilience. Read more.
body_text: Identity is the control plane of your business. When users can’t sign in, applications lose trust or policies stop working correctly. The impact is immediate. Microsoft detects an average of 38 million identity threats per day , underscoring why identity resilience has become a foundational part of business continuity planning. Protecting your identity framework should be the first step in resilience planning, and that’s why Microsoft’s new native Entra backup and recovery capability is such an important development. It represents meaningful progress in helping organizations recover identity data faster after an incident, especially when time matters most. A question customers ask is, “If Microsoft can back up my Entra ID data, why do I still need AvePoint?” Rather than viewing native recovery and third-party backup as competing approaches, the strongest resilience strategy is one that brings both together: Microsoft’s native recovery speed combined with AvePoint’s broader protection, longer retention, and operational flexibility. Together, they help organizations recover faster, bring back your Minimum Viable Company, and better align identity protection to real-world business and compliance needs. What Microsoft’s Native Solution Brings to the Table Microsoft’s native Entra ID recovery capability is designed to help restore identity data quickly at scale. This solution was built with one thing in mind – speed. For organizations facing a large-scale data loss event, that speed can be incredibly valuable. Microsoft’s solution, like AvePoint’s, helps to protect core Entra ID objects such as: Users Groups Applications Access Policies Named Locations Authentication Method Policies For the right recovery scenario, native recovery offers a fast path to getting critical identity services back online. In situations where mass recovery is the goal, where speed and continuity need to be prioritized first, this new functionality is essential. Native Entra ID backup was purpose-built for mass data loss scenarios and for large, enterprise-sized tenants. In scenarios where organizations need to recover a large number of objects and need to do so quickly, Microsoft’s first-party offering is a very compelling option. What Native Entra ID Backup Doesn’t Cover Native recovery is a strong foundation, but it was optimized for speed and for large-scale data loss scenarios. Comprehensive Entra ID protection requires more than speed alone. That’s where Cloud Backup for Entra ID starts to extend native capabilities. 1. Protected Objects Native protection was designed to protect a core selection of Entra ID objects, with a greater focus on the identity graph and policies that make up Entra. There are, however, more components that make up a full Entra ID environment, components that AvePoint’s solution can protect. For full Entra ID coverage, neither solution is enough in isolation — customers need both native and AvePoint Cloud Backup for Entra ID: Object Native Entra ID Backup AvePoint Cloud Backup User ✅ ✅ Group ✅ ✅ Application ✅ ✅ Service Principal ✅ ✅ Authentication Process ✅ ✅ Conditional Access Policies ✅ ✅ Named Location Policies ✅ ✅ Authorization Policies ✅ ❌ Administrative Units ❌ ✅ Roles and Administrators ❌ ✅ Devices ❌ ✅ BitLocker Recovery Keys can be protected with Cloud Backup Audit Logs and Sign-In Logs ❌ ✅ 2. Deleted Objects Recovery Native recovery for Entra ID objects is limited to those that have only been modified or that have been “soft-deleted”. That’s to say, any objects that have been deleted but still exist in your recycle bin. Anything that has been “hard deleted” – removed from the recycle bin – cannot be recovered with the native feature. AvePoint Cloud Backup supports recovery of objects regardless of their status. Even if Entra ID objects were deleted months ago, AvePoint’s solution can help you recover the exact version you need. 3. Backup Frequency and Scheduling Native Entra backup restricts organizations to a single backup job per day. For those massive data loss scenarios, this isn’t a dealbreaker; when recovering mass amounts of data, speed is often favored over granularity and flexibility. For operational recovery, though, once-daily backups may not be enough. Identity data changes constantly, and users or applications can have multiple versions within a 24-hour period. That’s why AvePoint Cloud Backup supports up to four incremental backup jobs per day. When it comes to day-to-day restores, the ability to choose specific versions of an object makes all the difference. 4. Retention Limitations With the native solution, customers can retain up to seven days of backup history. When it comes to disaster recovery, that limited retention is usually enough. If you’re rolling back entire tenants or recovering thousands of objects, you often don’t need to go back in time more than a day or two. However, for organizations with long-term retention requirements, this doesn’t fit the bill. AvePoint Cloud Backup supports flexible retention for Entra ID data, from one year to unlimited retention, depending on how the deal was structured. Customers with strict retention requirements, whether based on regulatory compliance or internal preferences, can hold onto data for as long as needed. 5. Independent Copy and Storage Flexibility Native Entra backup stores backup copies within the Microsoft trust, in the same geo-location as the protected Entra tenant. This helps the solution achieve faster recovery speeds, but it means there is no independent copy of data outside of Microsoft’s infrastructure. With AvePoint Cloud Backup, customers have their backup stored in a separate location. The solution supports AvePoint-hosted storage options (Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, or Amazon S3), as well as customer hosted Bring Your Own Storage (BYOS) support for the following storage types: Microsoft Azure Blob Storage Amazon S3 Storage Amazon S3-Compatible Storage FTP SFTP IBM Storage Protect - S3 IBM Cloud Object Storage Google Cloud Storage This independent backup copy, when paired with native Entra protection, can be an essential piece of regulatory compliance. With this, customers can more easily implement a 3-2-1 backup strategy for their critical identity data. Speed from Microsoft. Depth and Flexibility from AvePoint. Express Protection with Both. Entra data is some of the most critical in a modern enterprise. Often, the first point of entry for an attacker is an organization’s identity deployment, and because identity often governs access to the rest of the cloud environment, many recovery plans – including the AvePoint Rapid Recovery System – prioritize restoring identity services early on. That’s why organizations shouldn’t think about AvePoint vs Native for Entra protection. There doesn’t need to be a tradeoff between speed and flexibility. In practice, most organizations need a combination of capabilities: Fast recovery for large-scale incidents Granular restore options for everyday operational issues Longer retention for audit, investigation, and compliance Broader object and attribute coverage A consistent recovery experience across workloads This broad coverage and the ability to confidently recover from any type of Entra outage only comes when AvePoint Cloud Backup and Native Entra protection work together. AvePoint and Native Integration: The Better Together Story in Action Most organizations do not want to choose between recovery speed and recovery flexibility. They want access to both. That's why AvePoint Cloud Backup for Entra ID has integrated directly with Native Entra Recovery to bring the Express Recovery story to identity workloads. Rather than forcing administrators to work across multiple consoles and disconnected recovery workflows, AvePoint can surface native Microsoft recovery points directly within the Cloud Backup solution, allowing teams to see and leverage both protection layers from a single interface. Organizations using both solutions have the freedom to choose their recovery point and restore strategy based on their needs: Use Entra Express Recovery for large-scale data loss events and rapid recovery Use AvePoint Cloud Backup for day-to-day recovery, independent data copies, and long-term retention Use Both for fast rollback, 3-2-1 style backup strategies, and complete Entra resilience By bringing native Microsoft recovery points and AvePoint Cloud Backup together in a single experience, organizations no longer have to choose between recovery speed and recovery flexibility. Instead, they gain a recovery strategy that combines Microsoft's speed with AvePoint's depth, delivering a more resilient approach to protecting the identity layer that modern business depends on.

title: Dropshipping in Islamabad & Rawalpindi
summary: Start dropshipping in Islamabad & Rawalpindi with no investment — what sells, where to source, how COD and delivery work, and how to price for profit.
body_text: Dropshipping in Islamabad and Rawalpindi works like it does across Pakistan, with one local edge: the twin cities sit on the country's densest courier and cash-on-delivery network, so orders move quickly and COD collection is reliable. You don't need a shop, stock or upfront investment. You pick products from a wholesale supplier, share them with buyers in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and beyond, and the supplier ships each order cash-on-delivery while you keep the margin. This guide covers how to start from the twin cities, which products sell here, where to source them, how COD and delivery work locally, the pricing maths that keeps each order profitable, and the mistakes that cost new resellers money. How dropshipping works from the twin cities The model is the same whether you're in F-10, Saddar or Bahria Town. You don't buy stock. You list a supplier's products at your own price, share them on WhatsApp, Facebook or Instagram, and when someone orders you place that order with the supplier. They pack it, ship it to your customer, collect the cash on delivery, and pay you the difference. Your only job is finding buyers and pricing well. Because there's no inventory, your risk on each product stays at zero until a customer has already agreed to buy. You never carry dead stock, and you never pay for a product before you've sold it. That's what makes dropshipping realistic for a student in H-11 or someone selling part-time from a job in Blue Area. If you're brand new to the model, our step-by-step on how to start dropshipping in Pakistan without investment walks through the exact setup end to end. Why Islamabad and Rawalpindi are a strong base to sell from Three things make the twin cities easy to sell from. First, courier coverage: every major logistics company runs pickup across Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and delivery to the rest of Pakistan is typically 3–5 days. Nothing about your location slows fulfilment down. Second, buyers here are used to ordering online and paying cash on delivery, which keeps conversion high because customers pay only when the parcel arrives at their door. Third, you sit between two cities with different buyer profiles, and that widens your pool without any extra effort. A single product you post reaches Blue Area office workers, students in the university belt, and Raja Bazaar shoppers in the same feed. If you want to understand the wider opportunity and how resellers across the country operate, our overview for a reseller in Pakistan lays out the full picture. Step by step: setting up in the twin cities 1. Pick a niche you can speak to Start with something you actually understand or use. If you follow local fashion, sell ladies' wear. If you're into phones, sell mobile accessories. Knowing the product means you answer buyer questions fast, and fast replies close sales. Pick one narrow niche first rather than listing everything. 2. Choose a supplier you can trust Your supplier decides your delivery speed, return handling and payout reliability, so vet them before you list a single item. Check their catalogue price, minimum order, delivery coverage and how they pay you. A useful starting point is the Markaz supplier directory , and our guide to the best dropshipping suppliers in Pakistan explains exactly what to look for. 3. List products at your own price Browse a live wholesale catalogue, note the price you buy at, and set your resale price above it. On the Markaz shop every product shows the wholesale rate and a suggested retail range, so you can see your margin before you post. Sort by product category to find items that match your niche. 4. Market to local buyers Share your listings where twin-city buyers already are: WhatsApp status, Facebook Marketplace, local buy-and-sell groups, and short TikTok or Instagram Reels showing the product in use. Mention COD clearly — it's the single biggest reason a hesitant buyer says yes. 5. Fulfil the order and collect COD When a buyer confirms, place the order with your supplier at their address. The supplier ships it, the courier collects the cash, and your margin is remitted to you. You never handle stock or chase payment yourself. What sells well in Islamabad and Rawalpindi Local demand leans toward a few reliable categories. Winter is strong for warmers, jackets, thermal wear and home-heating accessories, because the twin cities get genuinely cold from November to February — this is the clearest seasonal window in the country. Year-round, ladies' fashion and accessories, mobile gadgets, kitchen and home tools, beauty items, and kids' products move steadily. A practical way to choose is to open the shop categories and see what's already listed and selling, then pick the sub-niche you can market best. Don't spread across ten categories on day one; win one, then widen. Where to source: local markets vs no-minimum app vs China-direct Local wholesale markets Raja Bazaar in Rawalpindi and the nearby wholesale lanes still offer the cheapest per-unit rate if you buy in bulk. The trade-offs are real: you pay cash up front, you travel and inspect each piece, and whatever doesn't sell is your loss. For a reseller testing several products, buying a dozen of each turns a small budget into inventory risk before the first sale. No-minimum wholesale apps This route fits how most resellers actually work: sell first, buy second. With a no-minimum supplier you order a single unit only after a customer has paid, cash-on-delivery, with your margin paid out to you. No upfront stock, no dead inventory. The per-piece rate sits close to what the markets charge for dozens, because the platform buys at volume and passes the tier down. The Markaz shop runs on exactly this model. China-direct for products Pakistan doesn't make For gadgets, novelty items and trend products that local markets don't carry, China-direct sourcing wins — but only when you count the landed cost, not the sticker price. Agent commission, freight, customs and local delivery all sit between the factory and your customer's door. Markaz China shortcuts that: the price you see is the landed, door-to-door rate, typically 10–17 days with no minimum order, and you can browse China deals by budget to stay within a price band. Our note on China to Pakistan delivery time explains the timelines in detail. Pricing and margin: a worked example Price to the market, not to your cost. Check what a product sells for on local pages and marketplaces, subtract your all-in cost including delivery, and only list items that leave a clear margin. Example numbers for a winter shawl: your wholesale cost is PKR 700, delivery is included, and similar shawls sell locally for PKR 1,200–1,400. List at PKR 1,299 and you keep roughly PKR 500–600 per order after cost. Aim for at least PKR 200–500 net per order so returns and the occasional undelivered parcel don't wipe out your profit. Because a no-minimum supplier ships one unit at a time, your startup budget can be close to zero — your real investment is the time spent posting and replying. We work through the full numbers in how much money you need to start dropshipping in Pakistan . COD, delivery timelines and returns Cash on delivery is the default in Pakistan and it's the biggest trust lever you have — buyers who won't prepay will happily order COD. The supplier handles collection and remits your margin, so you never chase payments. Local Islamabad and Rawalpindi orders are often next-day; the rest of Pakistan is typically 3–5 days. Returns are the trade-off with COD: some parcels come back undelivered, which is normal, so price for it rather than fearing it. Our guide to COD dropshipping in Pakistan covers how collection, remittance and returns actually work so the model stays cash-flow positive. Marketing to twin-city buyers You don't need ad spend to start. The cheapest channels convert best here: post the product on your WhatsApp status daily, list it on Facebook Marketplace and local Islamabad and Rawalpindi buy-and-sell groups, and record a 15-second Reel or TikTok showing it in use. Reference familiar areas — delivery to Saddar, G-11, Bahria Town, DHA — so buyers feel it's local and reliable. Reply within minutes; in COD selling, the fastest responder usually gets the order. Once a product sells consistently, put a small budget behind the post that's already working rather than guessing with a new one. Common mistakes to avoid A few errors sink new resellers. Listing too many products at once, so you can't answer questions on any of them. Pricing at cost-plus-a-little instead of to the market, leaving no room for returns. Ignoring return rates until they eat the month's profit. And picking a supplier on price alone — a cheap rate with slow delivery or poor return handling costs more than it saves. Vet the supplier first; the best dropshipping suppliers in Pakistan guide shows how to spot a reliable one and avoid scams. Quick answers Can I start dropshipping in Islamabad or Rawalpindi with no money? Yes. With a no-minimum, cash-on-delivery supplier you don't buy stock upfront — you only order after a customer has paid, so the startup cost is close to zero. How long does delivery take from the twin cities? Local Islamabad and Rawalpindi orders are often next-day, and delivery to the rest of Pakistan is typically 3–5 days through standard couriers. What sells best in Islamabad and Rawalpindi? Winter wear and heating accessories in the cold months, and year-round ladies' fashion, mobile gadgets, kitchen and home tools, and kids' items. Do I need to register a business to start? No. You can start as an individual reseller sharing products and collecting orders. Formal registration only becomes worthwhile once your volume grows. Is it better to source locally or from China? Source locally for fast-moving basics you can buy near Raja Bazaar, and go China-direct for gadgets and trend items Pakistan doesn't make — comparing landed cost, not sticker price.

title: Reimagining Public Safety: Data, Trust and Community Outcomes
summary: SoundThinking's Ralph Clark and Savannah Mayor Van Johnson discuss gun violence data gaps, staffing shortages, and rebuilding community trust.
body_text: Public safety leaders are being asked to do more with less and pulled in many directions. Reduce gun violence. Increase transparency. Adhere to new laws. Update technology. Stay within budget. Figure out service levels without additional staff. Keep communities safe. That was the backdrop for a fireside chat at the 2026 NBC-LEO Summer Conference in Birmingham, Alabama, where SoundThinking President and CEO Ralph Clark sat down with Mayor Van R. Johnson II, 1st Vice President of the National League of Cities and Mayor of Savannah, Georgia. Mayor Johnson started his career as a police officer, which gave the conversation a perspective that mixed policy with lived experience on patrol. The discussion covered a lot of ground, and the recap will cover some of the main dialogue, along with some of Mayor Johnson's most direct answers from the stage. The Data Gap Behind Gun Violence Clark opened by framing why SoundThinking exists in the first place. Over 80 percent of criminal gunfire goes unreported in the communities most affected by gun violence. That gap means police departments are often working without a clear picture of what is actually happening on their streets. While technology, especially gunshot detection technology , helps complete the full picture of gun violence in an area, Clark was careful to note that technology alone will not fix public safety. It takes leadership, collaboration, and trust between residents and the agencies serving them. Balancing People and Technology Amid a Staffing Crisis Mayor Johnson described a law enforcement hiring landscape that has turned into a bidding war. In his home county, more than 20 different police agencies compete for the same pool of officers through retention bonuses and lateral transfer incentives. That shortage has pushed departments to rely more heavily on technology as a force multiplier, not a replacement for personnel. "Job number one is public safety. If folks are not safe, you cannot be effective," Mayor Johnson said. He connected staffing pressure directly to the need for smarter deployment of resources. "You have to have knowledge-informed policing. You have to have what's called predictive policing, because sometimes we can really mess up by not having the right resources in the right place at the right time." When State Law Works Against Local Safety One of the most candid parts of the conversation covered Georgia's constitutional carry law and the state preemption fights that follow it. Mayor Johnson pointed to a striking statistic from Savannah: more than 240 guns were stolen from unlocked cars in one year –– no broken windows, no forced entry, just an open door. Savannah passed a local ordinance encouraging residents to lock their cars. The state legislature moved to override it. "We're fighting not only the perennial trigger pullers in the street, we're also fighting state governments and threats of preemption from people who will charge us to say, 'Well, you got to keep your community safe, but we're not going to give you the tools to do it,'" Mayor Johnson said. On the broader tension between gun rights and public safety, he put it plainly. "I believe we can protect the Second Amendment and protect second graders at the same time." The Human Cost Beyond the Statistics Clark shared a story from early in his career at SoundThinking, a ride-along in Baltimore where he responded to the scene of a homicide involving a teenager. What struck him most was not the scene itself, but the reaction of the young people standing nearby. There wasn't one. They had seen it before. Clark also connected that desensitization to outcomes that rarely show up in crime statistics: academic performance, teen pregnancy, early substance use, and untreated trauma. "It's all connected," he said. Growing up in Brooklyn, he described reaching a point where he stopped consciously hearing gunshots because he had heard them so often. He tied that same desensitization to undiagnosed post-traumatic stress disorder across entire neighborhoods. Rebuilding Trust at the Block Level During audience Q&A, an audience member turned to a solution that has nothing to do with technology: block captain programs, where trained residents watch out for their own streets and pass along what they know. "Neighborhoods instead of hoods. Put the neighbor back in the hood, that's what I'm talking about," he said. He was direct about why this matters. Police typically respond after a crime happens, not before it. An audience member also stated, "Because the police, if we're honest, they only come after something happens. They're not there to prevent it." Rebuilding that kind of community accountability, he said, means giving residents the confidence to act, even when it involves calling out their own neighbors. Putting that unity back in community really requires us to really create a situation where people feel empowered, and they feel protected in acting. Mayor Van R. Johnson II 1st Vice President, National League of Cities Public Safety as an Ecosystem, Not Just Policing The Takeaway The final audience question asked Mayor Johnson to separate policing culture from public safety as a system. His answer widened the lens considerably. "If we talk about public safety and only align it with police, we're missing the whole point. Public safety is police, it's fire, it's community services, it's all of those things. It's an ecosystem." He was equally candid about what cities do not control once an arrest is made, including prosecutors and judges. That is where he sees data playing its biggest role, not just in identifying where gun violence happens, but in building cases strong enough to keep repeat offenders off the street. "We now could dial up a map of saying, these are the gunshots, and these are the events on this date and this time over this period of time that is attributed to this person, which is why he doesn't need to be on our streets. That is technology that we did not have before." Neither Clark nor Mayor Johnson framed technology as a silver bullet. The conversation kept returning to the same idea: public safety improves when data, community trust, and local leadership work together instead of competing for credit. Technologies like gunshot detection are tools that allow public safety agencies to be more data-driven and strategic when making decisions. Staffing shortages, under-resourced neighborhoods, budgetary constraints, and other issues cannot be solved by technology. But technology is a tool that can give public safety leaders the information they need to make decisions that keep their communities safe. Learn more about how gunshot detection and data-informed strategies are helping cities reduce gun violence. Contact Us

title: Protara Therapeutics Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides a Business Update
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Protara Therapeutics, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Press Release Protara Therapeutics Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides a Business Update August 11, 2026 PDF Version Expect to complete enrollment of the BCG-Unresponsive registrational cohort of the ADVANCED-2 trial in 4Q 2026 The ADVANCED-3 trial is being redesigned as an exploratory trial to expand into and accelerate data in high-grade, high-risk BCG-Naïve and BCG-Exposed CIS (± Ta/T1) patients and papillary (Ta/T1) patients across BCG exposures Expect to provide an update and complete enrollment of the STARBORN-1 trial in LMs in 4Q 2026; expect to submit a Biologics License Application for TARA-002 in LMs in 2H 2027 On track to report interim results from THRIVE-3 registrational trial of IV Choline Chloride in patients dependent on long-term parenteral support in 4Q 2026 Cash, cash equivalents and investments of approximately $162 million as of June 30, 2026, expected to support planned operations into 2028 NEW YORK, Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Protara Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TARA), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing transformative therapies for the treatment of cancer and rare diseases, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 and provided a business update. “In the second quarter, we strengthened our late-stage pipeline through continued operational execution, positioning us for multiple important milestones over the coming quarters,” said Jesse Shefferman, Chief Executive Officer at Protara Therapeutics. “We continue to make progress in the ADVANCED-2 trial and expect to complete enrollment in the fourth quarter of 2026. We remain confident that TARA-002 will be a preferred treatment option in the non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) BCG-Unresponsive setting, and we are redesigning ADVANCED-3 to be a multi-cohort, open-label, exploratory trial, which will allow us to study TARA-002 in a broader high-grade, high-risk NMIBC patient population. The redesigned ADVANCED-3 protocol is expected to accelerate and expand the breadth of data available at or around the time of the potential launch of TARA-002 in BCG-Unresponsive carcinoma in situ (CIS) patients.” Mr. Shefferman added, “We also advanced our rare disease programs during the quarter. We recently presented encouraging interim durability and safety data from the STARBORN-1 pivotal trial of TARA-002 in Lymphatic Malformations (LMs) and, following discussions with the FDA, expect to submit our Biologics License Application (BLA) in the second half of 2027. At the same time, enrollment in the THRIVE-3 registrational trial evaluating IV Choline Chloride continues as planned, with interim results expected in the fourth quarter of this year. As we continue to execute across our portfolio, we believe we are well positioned to deliver a series of important clinical, regulatory and operational catalysts that have the potential to create meaningful value for patients and shareholders.” Recent Progress and Highlights TARA-002 in NMIBC The Company expects to complete enrollment of the BCG-Unresponsive cohort in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Company is redesigning the recently initiated ADVANCED-3 trial to be a multi-cohort, open-label, exploratory trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravesical TARA-002 in high-grade, high-risk BCG-Naïve and BCG-Exposed CIS ( ± Ta/T1) patients and papillary (Ta/T1) patients across BCG exposures. Importantly, this new design allows Protara to accelerate and expand the breadth of TARA-002 data in a broader high-grade, high-risk NMIBC patient population. TARA-002 in LMs Protara presented updated interim safety and durability data from the ongoing Phase 2 STARBORN-1 trial evaluating TARA-002 in pediatric patients with macrocystic and mixed cystic LMs in a poster session at the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies World Congress in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. As of an April 10, 2026 data cutoff: TARA-002 demonstrated clinical success in 83% (10/12) of participants that completed treatment and in 100% (10/10) of evaluable patients. All seven participants that reached the 32-week post-treatment assessment remained disease free as of the data cutoff. The majority of AEs were mild to moderate, with no serious AEs reported. The most common AEs were swelling and fatigue, and most were transient and resolved within a few days. Based on engagement with the FDA under Breakthrough Therapy designation, the Company intends to submit a BLA for TARA-002 in LMs based on the results of the pivotal STARBORN-1 trial in the second half of 2027 and will continue to submit safety and efficacy data from the trial on an ongoing basis to support the FDA’s evaluation of the risks and benefits of TARA-002 in LMs. IV Choline Chloride for Patients on Parenteral Support (PS) THRIVE-3, the Company’s registrational Phase 3 clinical trial, is ongoing, and the Company expects to report interim results in the fourth quarter of 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results As of June 30, 2026, unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and marketable debt securities totaled $161.9 million. The Company expects its cash and cash equivalents and marketable debt securities will be sufficient to fund its planned operations and milestones into 2028. Research and development expenses for the second quarter of 2026 increased to $17.0 million from $10.8 million for the prior year period. This increase was primarily due to higher direct costs associated with ongoing clinical trials of $3.2 million, increased personnel-related expenses of $1.8 million and increased non-program specific research and development expenses, primarily attributable to chemistry, manufacturing and controls of $1.2 million. General and administrative expenses for the second quarter of 2026 increased to $6.4 million from $5.8 million for the prior-year period. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel-related expenses of $0.7 million, offset by a decrease in other general and administrative expenses of $0.1 million. For the second quarter of 2026, Protara incurred a net loss of $21.7 million, or $0.36 per share, compared with a net loss of $15.0 million, or $0.35 per share, for the prior-year period. About TARA-002 TARA-002 is an investigational cell therapy in development for the treatment of NMIBC and of LMs, for which it has been granted Rare Pediatric Disease, Orphan Drug, Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA. TARA-002 is a first-in-class TLR2/NOD2 agonist and novel immunopotentiator derived from inactivated Streptococcus pyogenes with a mechanism of action that includes the activation of innate and adaptive immune pathways within the bladder wall. When TARA-002 is administered, it is hypothesized that innate and adaptive immune cells within the cyst or tumor are activated and produce a pro-inflammatory response with the release of cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, interferon (IFN)-gamma, IL-6, IL-10 and IL-12. TARA-002 also directly kills tumor cells and triggers a host immune response by inducing immunogenic cell death, which further enhances the antitumor immune response. TARA-002 was developed from the same master cell bank of genetically distinct group A Streptococcus pyogenes as OK-432, a broad immunopotentiator marketed as Picibanil® in Japan by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. About Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer Bladder cancer is the sixth most common cancer in the United States, with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) representing approximately 80% of bladder cancer diagnoses, or approximately 65,000 patients in the U.S. each year. NMIBC is cancer found in the tissue that lines the inner surface of the bladder that has not spread into the bladder muscle. Patients suffering from high-grade, high-risk NMIBC face high rates of disease recurrence and are potentially subject to full removal of the bladder (cystectomy). About Lymphatic Malformations Lymphatic Malformations (LMs) are rare, congenital malformations of lymphatic vessels resulting in the failure of these structures to connect or drain into the venous system. Protara’s focus is on macrocystic and mixed cystic LMs, for which there are no currently approved therapies. More than 50% of LMs are detected at birth and 90% diagnosed before the age of three years. The most common morbidities and serious manifestations of the disease include compression of the upper aerodigestive tract, including airway obstruction requiring intubation and possible tracheostomy dependence; intralesional bleeding; impingement on critical structures, including nerves, vessels and lymphatics; recurrent infection; and cosmetic and other functional disabilities. TARA-002 has been granted Rare Pediatric Disease, Orphan Drug, Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA for the treatment of LMs. About IV Choline Chloride for Patients on Parenteral Support IV Choline Chloride is an investigational, intravenous phospholipid substrate replacement therapy in development for patients receiving parenteral support (PS). Choline is an important substrate for phospholipids that are critical for healthy liver function and play an important role in modulating gene expression, cell membrane signaling, brain development and neurotransmission, muscle function and bone health. There are currently no available PS formulations containing choline. IV Choline Chloride has the potential to become the first FDA approved IV choline formulation for PS patients. It has been granted Orphan Drug designation by the FDA for the prevention and/or treatment of choline deficiency in patients on long-term parenteral nutrition and has been granted Fast Track designation as a source of choline when oral or enteral nutrition is not possible, insufficient or contraindicated. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has issued Protara a U.S. patent claiming a choline composition and a U.S. patent claiming a method of treating choline deficiency with a choline composition, each with a term expiring in 2041. About Protara Therapeutics, Inc. Protara is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to advancing transformative therapies for people with cancer and rare diseases. Protara’s portfolio includes its lead candidate, TARA-002, an investigational cell-based therapy in development for the treatment of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) and lymphatic malformations (LMs). The Company is evaluating TARA-002 in ongoing clinical trials in NMIBC patients with carcinoma in situ (CIS) who are unresponsive or naïve to treatment with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin, as well as a pivotal Phase 2 trial in pediatric patients with LMs. Additionally, Protara is developing IV Choline Chloride, an investigational phospholipid substrate replacement for patients on parenteral support who are otherwise unable to meet their choline needs via oral or enteral routes. For more information, visit www.protaratx.com .
